papers.title: The Aging Microenvironment Is a Determinant of Immune Exclusion and Metastatic Fate in Pancreatic Cancer.
papers.did: Used an age-relevant syngeneic orthotopic model of pancreatic cancer and heterochronic co-implantation to test how organismal and stromal aging affect tumor progression, metastasis, and immune infiltration.
papers.found: Organismal aging accelerated PDAC progression and metastasis; young CAFs restored immune infiltration and reduced metastasis in aged hosts, while aged CAFs failed to enhance metastasis in young hosts.
papers.used: Age-relevant syngeneic orthotopic PDAC model, transcriptomic and secretome profiling, heterochronic co-implantation models.
papers.why: Establishes stromal aging as a driver of immune exclusion and metastasis, suggesting rejuvenation of the aged tumor microenvironment could improve outcomes in older PDAC patients.
papers.anchor_quote: organismal aging accelerates PDAC progression and metastasis.

papers.title: Organellar pH as an emerging vulnerability to exploit in cancer.
papers.did: Reviews the mechanisms cancer cells use to maintain intracellular pH homeostasis, focusing on organellar pH regulation, and assesses inhibitors of the transporters involved in organellar acidification.
papers.found: An alkaline intracellular pH gives cancer cells a survival advantage by promoting proliferation, migration, and resistance to cell death.
papers.used: Literature review of pH-regulating membrane transporters and organellar acidification pathways in cancer.
papers.why: Highlights organellar acidification as a potential therapeutic vulnerability that could be targeted pharmacologically in cancer.
papers.anchor_quote: an alkaline pH i provides cancer cells with a survival advantage by promoting their proliferation, migration, and resistance to cell death.

papers.title: PI5P4Kα promotes glucose and iron acquisition to support metabolic fitness in pancreatic cancer.
papers.did: Investigated the role of the phosphoinositide kinase PI5P4Kα in supporting glucose and iron acquisition in pancreatic cancer cells, including inhibition studies and a xenograft mouse model.
papers.found: PI5P4Kα inhibition creates a metabolic bottleneck causing cancer-specific apoptotic death that is reversible by iron supplementation, and PI5P4Kα knockdown suppresses tumor growth in a PDAC xenograft model.
papers.used: Xenograft mouse model of PDAC, loss-of-function/knockdown experiments, metabolic substrate acquisition assays.
papers.why: Positions PI5P4Kα as a promising therapeutic target for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
papers.anchor_quote: PI5P4Kα knockdown suppresses tumor growth in a xenograft mouse model of PDAC.

papers.title: Macropinocytosis maintains CAF subtype identity under metabolic stress in pancreatic cancer.
papers.did: Studied how macropinocytosis maintains the myCAF phenotype in cancer-associated fibroblasts under glutamine-limited metabolic stress in PDAC, including in vivo blockade experiments.
papers.found: Blocking macropinocytosis in vivo drives myCAF-to-iCAF transitions, reducing collagen and increasing immune infiltration and vascular expansion, which sensitizes PDAC tumors to immunotherapy and chemotherapy.
papers.used: In vivo PDAC models, macropinocytosis inhibition, MEK-ERK signaling analysis.
papers.why: Reveals a stromal-remodeling strategy that can improve immunotherapy and chemotherapy responses in pancreatic cancer.
papers.anchor_quote: stromal remodeling driven by macropinocytosis inhibition-including iCAF enrichment, collagen reduction, immune cell infiltration, and vascular expansion-sensitizes PDAC tumors to immunotherapy and chemotherapy.

papers.title: Disabling PSGL-1 abrogates immune suppression and resistance to PD-1 blockade in pancreatic cancer.
papers.did: Defined PSGL-1 as an immune checkpoint using a syngeneic orthotopic PDAC model with PSGL-1 knockout mice, examining T cell infiltration and response to PD-1 blockade.
papers.found: PSGL-1-/- mice showed T cell-dependent control of primary tumors and lung metastases, increased CD8+ T cell engagement, and a near complete response to therapeutic PD-1 blockade.
papers.used: Syngeneic orthotopic PDAC model, PSGL-1 knockout mice, spatial analysis of tumor immune infiltrates, PD-1 blockade therapy.
papers.why: Identifies PSGL-1 as a therapeutic target to limit CD8+ T cell exhaustion and enhance immunotherapy response in pancreatic cancer.
papers.anchor_quote: PSGL-1 -/- mice displayed striking T cell-dependent control of primary tumors and lung metastases.

papers.title: The Aging Microenvironment as a Determinant of Immune Exclusion and Metastatic Fate in Pancreatic Cancer.
papers.did: Preprint using an age-relevant syngeneic orthotopic PDAC model and heterochronic co-implantation to test how organismal and stromal aging affect tumor progression, metastasis, and immune infiltration.
papers.found: Organismal aging accelerated PDAC progression and metastasis; revitalizing aged tumor stroma with young CAFs restored immune infiltration and attenuated metastasis in older hosts, while aged CAFs did not enhance metastasis in young hosts.
papers.used: Age-relevant syngeneic orthotopic PDAC model, transcriptomic profiling, heterochronic co-implantation models.
papers.why: Establishes a conceptual framework for how aging shapes the PDAC tumor microenvironment, motivating therapeutic targeting of stromal aging.
papers.anchor_quote: we demonstrate that organismal aging accelerates PDAC progression and metastasis.

papers.title: MICAL2 Promotes Pancreatic Cancer Growth and Metastasis.
papers.did: Characterized the super-enhancer landscape of human PDAC and performed loss- and gain-of-function experiments to study MICAL2's role in tumor growth and metastasis.
papers.found: MICAL2 was overexpressed in PDAC and correlated with poor prognosis; it promoted ERK1/2 and AKT activation and macropinocytosis, and supported in vivo tumor growth and metastasis, with MRTF-B (not MRTF-A) phenocopying its effects.
papers.used: Super-enhancer landscape analysis, loss- and gain-of-function experiments in human and mouse PDAC cells, in vivo tumor models.
papers.why: Identifies MICAL2 as a super-enhancer-associated gene and potential pharmacologic target for pancreatic cancer.
papers.anchor_quote: MICAL2 supported in vivo tumor growth and metastasis.

papers.title: A hormetic response model for glutamine stress in cancer.
papers.did: Proposes a biphasic hormetic model to describe cellular stress responses to glutamine deprivation or targeting in cancer, synthesizing preclinical and clinical findings.
papers.used: Synthesis of preclinical and clinical literature on glutamine metabolism inhibition in cancer.
papers.why: Aims to guide future studies by anticipating hormetic effects of glutamine stress to improve clinical translation of glutamine-targeted therapies.
papers.anchor_quote: cellular stress responses to glutamine deprivation or targeting may be modeled as a biphasic hormetic response.

papers.title: Macropinocytosis controls metabolic stress-driven CAF subtype identity in pancreatic cancer.
papers.did: Preprint investigating how macropinocytosis controls CAF subtype identity under glutamine-limited metabolic stress in PDAC using in vivo models.
papers.found: Blocking macropinocytosis altered CAF subtypes and reorganized the tumor stroma in vivo, changes that could be exploited to sensitize PDAC to immunotherapy and chemotherapy.
papers.used: In vivo PDAC models, macropinocytosis inhibition, MEK/ERK signaling analysis.
papers.why: Shows metabolic stress shapes the tumor microenvironment in a way that can be harnessed therapeutically.
papers.anchor_quote: blocking macropinocytosis alters CAF subtypes and reorganizes the tumor stroma.

papers.title: Cell polarity proteins promote macropinocytosis in response to metabolic stress.
papers.did: Identified the atypical protein kinase C enzymes PKCζ and PKCι as regulators of macropinocytosis and studied their mechanism via the Par3/Par6 cell-polarity scaffold proteins.
papers.found: aPKCs are regulated by EGFR signaling or the transcription factor CREM to promote Par3 relocation to microtubules in a dynein-dependent manner; restoring macropinocytosis rescues fitness loss from aPKC depletion, and aPKCs support PDAC growth in vivo.
papers.used: Epithelial cell polarity models, aPKC/Par3/Par6 protein interaction studies, in vivo PDAC growth assays.
papers.why: Reveals a mechanistic link between cell-polarity machinery and nutrient scavenging that supports pancreatic cancer growth.
papers.anchor_quote: aPKCs support PDAC growth in vivo.

papers.title: Macropinocytosis and Cancer: From Tumor Stress to Signaling Pathways.
papers.did: Reviews the cellular stress stimuli known to induce macropinocytosis in cancer cells and the underlying molecular mechanisms.
papers.found: Cells harboring oncogene or tumor suppressor mutations display heightened macropinocytosis, enabling survival and proliferation despite nutrient-scarce tumor conditions.
papers.used: Literature review of macropinocytosis regulation across stress conditions in cancer.
papers.why: Synthesizes how macropinocytosis acts as an adaptive survival mechanism for cancer cells, informing future therapeutic strategies.
papers.anchor_quote: macropinocytosis is associated with cancer malignancy.

papers.title: Automated Imaging and Analysis for the Quantification of Fluorescently Labeled Macropinosomes.
papers.did: Describes an automated imaging and analysis method using a multi-mode plate reader to quantify macropinocytosis via fluorescent dextran uptake in adherent cells.
papers.found: The method enables rapid quantification of the macropinocytic index in 96-well microplates or on fixed coverslips with improved reproducibility and reduced experimental variation.
papers.used: High molecular weight fluorescent dextran uptake assay, automated multi-mode plate reader imaging, 96-well microplate format.
papers.why: Provides a time-saving, cost-effective, reproducible tool for identifying regulators of macropinocytosis and screening therapeutics.
papers.anchor_quote: rapid quantification of the macropinocytic index in adherent cells.

papers.title: The pervasiveness of macropinocytosis in oncological malignancies.
papers.did: Reviews the role of macropinocytosis as an amino acid supply route across various cancer types and its molecular drivers.
papers.found: Macropinocytosis is a pervasive feature across many tumor types and also serves as an entry mechanism for nanomedicine delivery.
papers.used: Literature review across multiple oncological malignancies and macropinocytosis-driven nanomedicine delivery mechanisms.
papers.why: Highlights macropinocytosis as both a metabolic vulnerability and a potential drug-delivery route across many cancers.
papers.anchor_quote: macropinocytosis represents a novel amino acid supply route that tumour cells use to survive the nutrient-poor conditions of the tumour microenvironment.
